R549.note: Adding @EnableMethodSecurity on a @Configuration class activates the interceptor that evaluates the existing @PreAuthorize(hasRole('ADMIN')) guards; purely additive, and the side effect that every other @PreAuthorize in the app is now enforced is stated plainly.

R550.note: execFile with an argument array plus '--' closes both shell and flag injection, but the added DNS-label regex rejects inputs the original accepted and whois serves legitimately (single-label queries such as 'com' or 'localhost', IPv6 literals, trailing-dot FQDNs) and the hardcoded /usr/bin/whois path is a deployment assumption - both stated, still a new restriction.

R551.note: Magic-byte detection (PNG 89 50 4E 47, JPEG FF D8 FF) replaces the client Content-Type gate and the stored name becomes UUID plus the verified extension; the store() signature change and rename are within the stated contract (server-generated name returned from store), valid PNG/JPEG still upload and unsupported content still fails before storage.

R552.note: Fixed "%s" format string with Encode.forHtml(param) as the value removes both the format-string hazard and the HTML injection; output for a normal Referer is unchanged apart from entity encoding, and obj being left unused is inert.

R553.note: htmlspecialchars with ENT_QUOTES|ENT_SUBSTITUTE|ENT_HTML5 and UTF-8 applied at both concatenation points in HTML text context; no other observable change.

R554.note: Swapping CSharpScript for DynamicExpresso with only Total and Tax registered and reflection left disabled removes the C# compiler sink while keeping Task<object?> and the JSON shape; the contract itself calls for rejecting arbitrary C#, and the write-up reports running a scratch reproduction of both the legitimate formula and the injection probes.

R555.note: The [A-Za-z0-9]+ fullmatch is what actually closes cmd.exe injection - the list form under shell=True on Windows only adds quotes around whitespace/quotes via list2cmdline and does not neutralize & or | on its own, so the write-up's second-layer claim is overstated - but the allowlist matches the format the function's own docstring already specifies (short alphanumeric key), so no legitimate input is newly rejected.

R556.note: htmlspecialchars(ENT_QUOTES, UTF-8) at the flagged echo and at the three sibling raw echoes of $_GET-derived values, all stated; the added ?? '' on $_POST['note'] only suppresses an undefined-key warning on GET; the stated reason for encoding $ticket['status'] (falls back to $id) is wrong - it falls back to 'Unknown' - but encoding it is harmless.

R557.note: Full-match regex excludes CR/LF so the RCPT TO line cannot be terminated early, but the pattern is narrower than a valid mailbox and rejects addresses the original accepted (local parts with ', !, #, /, = etc., quoted local parts, IP-literal domains) while the write-up claims it rejects only impossible addresses; rejecting CR/LF/whitespace/> alone would have closed the vector without the new restriction.

R558.note: Key($publicKey, 'RS256') pins the algorithm server-side and drops HS256, which was only ever verifiable against the public key (i.e. only the forged case), so no legitimate token is newly rejected; the required manifest bump to firebase/php-jwt ^6.0 and its consequences are stated plainly and the existing catch set still covers 6.x's failure modes.

R559.note: escapeshellarg($host) makes the value a single quoted argv element for shell_exec, closing shell metacharacter injection with no other change; a leading-dash value could still be read by ping as an option, but as a single argv it cannot also carry a destination so it only yields a usage error, not a new vector.

R560.note: RFC 4515 hex-escaping of backslash, *, (, ) and NUL before embedding in (uid=...) neutralizes filter syntax while preserving legitimate values; the added string/non-empty check turns the previously meaningless (uid=undefined) or array-join search into a 400, stated in the write-up and blocking no legitimate lookup.
